concepts.name: Function notation
concepts.description: f(a) means substitute x = a into the rule for f(x), and evaluate.

concepts.name: Domain restrictions
concepts.description: The domain excludes any input that would divide by zero or take the square root of a negative number.

concepts.name: Linear graphs
concepts.description: A line y = mx + c has slope m (how steep it is) and y-intercept c (where it crosses the y-axis).

concepts.name: Composing functions
concepts.description: (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)) means apply g first, then feed that result into f.

concepts.name: Inverse functions
concepts.description: The inverse of a linear function undoes it: swap x and y in the equation, then solve for y again.

formulas.title: Evaluating a function
formulas.formula: f(a) = substitute x = a into the expression for f(x)
formulas.explanation: The letter inside the brackets is not multiplication — it tells you which input value to substitute.

formulas.title: Finding a domain restriction
formulas.prompt: What values must be excluded from the domain of a function?
formulas.formula: Exclude x-values that make a denominator zero, or that make an expression under a square root negative
formulas.explanation: These are the two most common sources of domain restrictions for the functions met at this level.
formulas.example: f(x) = 1/(x − 4) is undefined at x = 4, so 4 is excluded from the domain
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to check for division by zero.
formulas.applicationPrompt: What value must be excluded from the domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 4)?

formulas.title: Slope-intercept form
formulas.prompt: What do m and c represent in y = mx + c?
formulas.formula:
y = mx + c
m = slope = rise/run = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
c = y-intercept (value of y when x = 0)
formulas.explanation: The slope tells you how much y changes for each unit increase in x; the intercept tells you where the line crosses the y-axis.
formulas.commonMistake: Reversing the numerator and denominator when computing slope.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the slope of the line through (2,5) and (6,13).

formulas.title: Composing two functions
formulas.explanation: Work from the inside out: evaluate the inner function first, then use that result as the input to the outer function.
formulas.commonMistake: Applying f before g, which reverses the intended order.
formulas.applicationPrompt: If f(x) = 2x+1 and g(x) = x−3, find f(g(5)).

formulas.title: Finding an inverse function
formulas.prompt: How do you find the inverse of a linear function y = mx + c?
formulas.formula: Swap x and y, then solve for y again: x = my + c  →  y = (x − c)/m
formulas.explanation: The inverse function undoes the original: applying f and then f⁻¹ (or vice versa) returns the original input.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to swap x and y before solving.

formulas.title: Check an inverse by composing
formulas.prompt: How can you check an inverse function you have found?
formulas.formula:
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x for every x
Try one number
formulas.explanation: The inverse undoes the function, so applying both must give back what you started with.
formulas.commonMistake: Taking the reciprocal 1/f(x) as the inverse.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Is (x − 5)/2 the inverse of 2x + 5? Check with x = 1.

formulas.title: Moving a graph
formulas.prompt: How do changes to the formula move a graph?
formulas.formula:
f(x) + k: up by k
f(x − h): right by h (note the minus)
−f(x): flipped over the x-axis
formulas.explanation: Changing the input shifts sideways, changing the output shifts up or down.
formulas.example: y = (x − 2)² + 3 is y = x² moved 2 right and 3 up, so its lowest point is (2, 3).
formulas.applicationPrompt: Where is the lowest point of y = (x + 4)² − 1?

levels.title: Functions as Input-Output Machines
levels.description: A function takes an input, applies a rule, and produces an output — f(a) means "the output when the input is a."

blocks.title: Substitute, don’t multiply
blocks.body: f(x) = 3x + 2 is a rule. f(4) does not mean f times 4 — it means substitute x = 4 into the rule: 3(4) + 2 = 14.

blocks.title: Evaluating a function
blocks.body: f(a) = substitute x = a into f(x)
blocks.caption: The value inside the brackets is the input, not a factor.

blocks.body: A denominator can never be zero — that is usually where a domain restriction comes from.

blocks.title: A graph is every input with its output
blocks.body:
Plot each input x against its output f(x) and you get the graph of f. Change the rule and the graph moves: f(x − h) + k is the same graph slid h across and k up, and a·f(x) stretches it.

Watch the input: f(x − 3) moves the graph 3 to the right, not the left, because x must be 3 bigger to give the same output.

hints.text: f(4) means substitute x = 4, not multiply f by 4.

questions.question: If f(x) = x² − 1, what is f(−3)?
questions.method: Square the whole value of x, including its sign.

questions.question: For a function f, the expression f(5) means
questions.explanation: f(5) tells you to substitute x = 5 into the rule for f(x) and evaluate the result.
questions.method: The bracket holds the input value, not a multiplier.

hints.text: Function notation is not the same as multiplication.

questions.question: What is the slope of the line y = 3x − 2?
questions.explanation: In y = mx + c, the coefficient of x is the slope, so the slope is 3.
questions.method: The slope is the coefficient of x.

hints.text: Match the equation to the form y = mx + c.

commonMistakes: Giving the y-intercept, −2, instead of the slope.

questions.question: What value must x avoid in the domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 4)?
questions.explanation: The denominator x − 4 cannot be zero, so x ≠ 4.
questions.method: A denominator can never equal zero.

hints.text: Set the denominator equal to zero to find the excluded value.

commonMistakes: Excluding the wrong value, such as 0.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x − 3, what is f(g(5))?
questions.method: Work from the inside out: apply g first, then f.

hints.text: Evaluate the inner function before the outer one.

questions.question: If f(x) = x² + 2x, what is f(3) − f(1)?
questions.method: Evaluate each value separately before subtracting.

hints.text: Compute f(3) and f(1) fully before subtracting.

commonMistakes: Subtracting inside the function first, computing f(3−1) instead.

questions.question: What is the slope of the line through (2, 5) and (6, 13)?
questions.method: Slope = rise over run, in the same order for both points.

hints.text: Keep the same point first in both subtractions.

commonMistakes: Subtracting the coordinates in a mismatched order.

questions.question: A line has slope 4 and passes through (1, 9). What is its y-intercept?
questions.explanation: Using y = 4x + c with (1,9): 9 = 4(1) + c, so c = 5.
questions.method: Substitute the known point into y = mx + c and solve for c.

hints.text: Substitute the given point into the slope-intercept equation.

commonMistakes: Assuming the given point is the y-intercept itself.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x + 6, what is f⁻¹(10)?
questions.explanation: The inverse is f⁻¹(x) = (x − 6)/2. So f⁻¹(10) = (10 − 6)/2 = 2.
questions.method: Find the inverse function first, then substitute.

hints.text: Swap x and y in the equation, then solve for y.

commonMistakes: Substituting 10 into f(x) instead of finding the inverse first.

questions.question: If f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x² + 1, what is g(f(2))?
questions.method: Apply f first (the inner function), then g.

hints.text: g(f(2)) means f is applied first.

questions.question: The points (1, 4) and (3, 10) lie on the line y = mx + c. What is m + c?
questions.method: Find the slope first, then substitute a point to find c.

hints.text: You need both m and c before you can add them.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to solve for c after finding m.

questions.question: A function f(x) = ax + b satisfies f(1) = 5 and f(3) = 13. What is f(10)?
questions.explanation: From the two equations: a + b = 5 and 3a + b = 13. Subtracting gives 2a = 8, so a = 4 and b = 1. Then f(10) = 4(10) + 1 = 41.
questions.method: Set up two equations from the two given values, solve for a and b, then evaluate.

hints.text: Treat f(1) = 5 and f(3) = 13 as a pair of simultaneous equations.

commonMistakes: Trying to guess a and b instead of solving for them.
